free_tier.stated: Free for everyone with no API key: articles, blogs and ISS reports from many spaceflight news sites, up to 500 results a request, 5 requests a second for anonymous callers.
free_tier.notes: No daily or monthly request quota is stated; the only published limit is the anonymous throttle of 5 requests a second. The importer checks for new data every 10 minutes. The project asks commercial users to consider supporting it through Patreon or a donation.

per_object_cap.stated: 500 results a request: a limit above 500 is answered with 500 results and a next link at limit=500
per_object_cap.notes: The offset parameter is at most 10,000; further back, filter on published_at_lt with the published_at of the last result.

retention.stated: the full archive is served: the article list counted 36741 articles when read

interface_detail: REST over HTTPS at api.spaceflightnewsapi.net/v4 (articles, blogs, reports, info) with an OpenAPI 3 schema at /v4/schema/, and a GraphQL endpoint at /v4/graphql/
tooling: any HTTP client or GraphQL client; the OpenAPI schema generates a client
chaining: Article, blog and report metadata with a summary, the source URL and Launch Library 2 launch and event ids; the full article is fetched from the source URL by a crawler.

limits.value: 5 requests a second for anonymous callers
a limit above 500 is clamped to 500 results a request
offset at most 10,000; filter on published_at_lt to go further back

binding_note: 5 requests a second is the only published limit; 36741 articles at 500 results a request is 74 requests (36741 / 500, rounded up).

identity_cost.detail: No account and no key: a plain GET answered HTTP 200 with articles.

reliability_note: Responses carry cache-control max-age 600; the throttle for anonymous callers is stated in the project changelog and was not exercised by a burst.
confidence_note: The no-key access and the page-size clamp were read from live answers; the 5 requests a second throttle is read from the project changelog and was not exercised, so the record stays documented.

evidence.proved: the API is free for everyone
evidence.quote: Yes, SNAPI is fully free to use for everyone.
No API key is required to use SNAPI.
The importer runs every 10 minutes to check for new data, so new articles can take up to 10 minutes to appear in the API.

evidence.proved: anonymous requests are throttled to 5 per second
evidence.quote: Update API throttling settings to limit anonymous requests to 5 per second

evidence.proved: the offset parameter is at most 10,000, with published_at_lt for going further
evidence.quote: The initial index from which to return the results, at most 10,000.

evidence.proved: a GraphQL endpoint is offered beside REST
evidence.quote: The Spaceflight News API also has GraphQL support available!

evidence.proved: a keyless GET answered with articles and counted 36741 of them
a request for limit=2000 was clamped: the next link is at limit=500

notes: Storage: no storage or caching limit is stated in the documentation or the FAQ. Bulk path: page the article list at limit=500 with offset up to 10,000, then filter on published_at_lt with the published_at of the last result; 74 requests cover 36741 articles.
